findings.element: The past block under [data-past="listed"] — b.css:381-383 with the <details> built in render-b.js behindBlock(); reached as ?v=record on every state, and as the printed keepsake
findings.problem: The round-2 disclosure was built, and in the one room whose entire promise is the past it shows nothing. Driven at 1440 on ?v=record&state=print and ?v=record&state=desk: .b-behindRow count is 3, rows passing checkVisibility is 0, .b-behindLabel visible is false, .b-behindCount visible is false. The rule [data-past="listed"] .b-behindSummary { display: none } hides the control, and because the h2 "Behind you" and the "3 moments" count live INSIDE that summary they are deleted with it; the two rules meant to compensate, [data-past="listed"] .b-behindRows { display: block }, cannot fire at all because .b-behindRows sits inside a <details> that is still closed, and Chromium hides closed content through ::details-content's content-visibility, which display on a child does not override. So the record room — whose own console copy reads "The long view · Everything that happened" — renders a hairline, no heading, and one floating sentence, and prints exactly that on the keepsake. It shows strictly LESS of the past than the approach room, where at least the rows can be asked for. The gate cannot see it: interaction-check.mjs:1135-1139 is the only assertion for this room and it asserts that the control is display:none, never that the rows are there — it passes precisely because the content is gone. Separately, ?v=approach&state=print prints a collapsed, unpressable disclosure onto paper, which the comment above these very rules says must never happen.
findings.fix: Stop fighting the element and open it at render time. (1) In render-b.js behindBlock(), read the mount root's data-past once, the same way the other named decisions are read, and set the open attribute on the <details> when it is "listed", so the rows genuinely render. (2) Move h2.b-behindLabel and span.b-behindCount OUT of <summary> and render them as the first children of section.b-behind, leaving the summary to carry only the affordance; then [data-past="listed"] .b-behindSummary { display: none } hides a control without taking a heading and a count with it. (3) Delete both [data-past="listed"] .b-behindRows rules at b.css:382-383 — they are inert, and they are the reason this read as fixed. (4) Replace the single assertion at interaction-check.mjs:1135-1139 with four, run over v=record at print, desk, phone and day: every .b-behindRow passes checkVisibility({contentVisibilityAuto:true}); .b-behindLabel is visible; the count text equals the rendered row count; and no <summary> is rendered. Reshoot the record room at all four widths.

findings.element: Owner bar, "Preview" and "Publish" (render-b.js wireOwner preview/publish branches) and the states they mount
findings.problem: Driven at 1440 from owner-flight: press Add a moment, type "Hair trial" — the row is on the measure and the bar reads "A moment was added." Press Preview. The desk that appears lists the seven original moments and no Hair trial. Press Back to the plan: the owner returns to a plan of seven rows, Hair trial gone, the reversibility bar silent and empty, nothing announced. The same happens to visibility, which is worse because it is the whole point of that control: mark "Send the invitations" as Hidden — the row and its accessible name both read "Hidden from guests" — then press Preview, and the preview shows Send the invitations to guests. Every state remounts from the fixture, so the one button whose job is "show me what they will see" is guaranteed to show something else, and the owner's most natural loop — change it, check it, come back — destroys the change silently on a plan people are waiting for. This is not the deck argument: add, delete, date, hide and undo are all built and all reversible WITHIN a state, and 357 assertions grade them. The gate never crosses a state boundary with an edit in hand.
findings.fix: Give the surface one working list. In render-b.js, hold the milestones in a module-level session array seeded from F.milestones on first mount; make add, delete, setAway and the visibility toggle mutate that array, and make every state's row builder and every derived count read it through the one accessor rather than re-reading the fixture. Preview then previews, Back to the plan returns to the edited plan, and publish's card counts the same list. If a session store is judged too large for this round, ship the smaller honest version instead, never nothing: in the preview and publish branches, when history.length > 0, refuse in place — write "Preview shows the plan as it was sent. Your changes are still on the plan." into the existing role=status bar, keep focus on the pressed button, and do not navigate. Either way add one line to states.publish beneath the card, from the same accessor: the count of visibility==="shown" against the total, so the screen that hands the plan over states what guests will actually get. Gate: assert that after Add a moment the previewed desk contains the added title, that a moment marked Hidden is absent from the previewed desk, and that Back to the plan returns the row count it left with.

findings.element: .b-behindSummary (b.css:323-334) — the single focusable element on phone, desk, print and day
findings.problem: Driven at 390: the whole guest artifact contains exactly one control, and nothing on it says so. .b-behindLabel and .b-behindCount are 11px mono, uppercase, var(--track-label), var(--fore-62) — identical in family, size, case, tracking and ink to .b-label, the class used for the inert section captions "DAYS AWAY", "HAPPENING NOW" and "TODAY IS 16 JULY". list-style is none and ::-webkit-details-marker is display:none, so there is no triangle, chevron or sign of any kind. There is no hover rule and no focus rule on the summary, though .b-grab two hundred lines above has both. The only state signal in the file is .b-behindDetails[open] .b-behindCount { color: var(--fore) } — the count brightens AFTER you have opened it, which is no help to someone deciding whether to try. On the wedding morning at 390 the guest sees two identically drawn micro-labels a centimetre apart, "HAPPENING NOW" and "HOW YOU GOT HERE · 8 MOMENTS"; one is a caption and one is the only door in the product, and nothing separates them. The behaviour gate proves the disclosure works when clicked; it cannot see that nobody would click it. The audit gate cannot see it either — its hit-target selector is button, a, [tabindex], input, textarea, select, so <summary> is never measured, and this one is 32px tall.
findings.fix: Draw it as a control. In b.css give .b-behindSummary a ::after carrying "+" in var(--mono) at 11px in var(--fore) — full-strength ink, so it separates from the fore-62 label beside it — sitting after .b-behindCount with an 8px gap, swapped to "−" under .b-behindDetails[open] .b-behindSummary::after inside the declared 0.14s cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1). Raise min-height from 32px to 44px and add padding: 8px; margin: 0 -8px; so the pressable band runs the full width of the measure on a phone. Add .b-behindSummary:hover { background: var(--fore-06) } — the token .b-grab already uses — and a :focus-visible ring routed through the same custom property .b-grab and .b-act use, declared after the state rules so specificity cannot kill it. Keep the 4px radius already set. Gate: assert the summary's rendered box is at least 44px tall at 390 on phone, desk and day; that a ::after with content renders in both the closed and the open state; and that its computed background changes on hover.

findings.element: .b-behindRow for item.state === "cancelled" (render-b.js behindBlock row builder; b.css:369)
findings.problem:
Open "Behind you" on the guest phone and the third row reads "No date · City hotel shortlist". Its full markup is No date

City hotel shortlist

. The only thing saying this is not happening is a line-through drawn in var(--fore-28) — a 28%-alpha rule through 15px text on a dark ground — and the row's accessible name carries no word for it at all, so a screen reader announces a live-sounding item and a sighted guest at arm's length on a phone reads one too. The one sentence that does state it, "The city hotel shortlist is not going ahead.", sits outside the disclosure and below it, and is read as separate prose. And "No date" describes the record rather than the event: a thing that was called off did not fail to have a date. This is the library's own class — state carried only visually, when the same fact must exist in words in the accessible name — reappearing in the one place a guest goes to check whether something is still on. The gate asserts that asking shows every row; it asserts nothing about what a row says.
findings.fix: Put the state in words in the row. In render-b.js's behindBlock row builder, when item.state === "cancelled" append a third child after the title — Not going ahead — styled in b.css on the existing label treatment (var(--mono), 11px, var(--track-label), uppercase, var(--fore-62)) so no new type step is introduced, and let the row's own text carry the fact. Keep the line-through as reinforcement only. Replace the "No date" cell on cancelled rows with an empty cell; .b-behindDate is a fixed 76px column, so the row stays aligned without it. While in the same function, settle the count rule the two clocks disagree on: line 220 excludes cancelled items on the day and includes them before it, so the same guest reads "3 moments" in July and "8 moments" in October with one item having quietly left the record — either keep cancelled items in both, now that the new word carries them, or drop them from both. Gate: assert every [data-cancelled="true"] row's textContent contains the state in words, and that the summary's count equals the number of rows rendered beneath it on both clocks.

findings.problem: Measured at 390x844 on owner-flight: the owner bar stacks to workspace line, identity capsule, Add a moment and Preview as a two-up, then Publish full width — roughly 380px of chrome before any content. The first moment lands at y=792 and exactly 1 of 7 rows is on the first screen. The same plan on the guest phone at the same width puts the first moment at y=540 with 3 of 7 visible. So the owner, the person who needs to see the shape of the plan most often, gets the worst view of it, and what outranks it is three buttons, one of which they press once ever. The most important thing on the screen is not the most prominent thing, and on a phone it is not on the screen at all. Frames at 1440 hide this completely; the gate asserts the controls exist and work, never where they sit relative to the thing they act on.
findings.fix: Below the 701px breakpoint b.css already uses, take .b-barActs out of .b-bar and render it as a fixed bottom action row of three — Add a moment, Preview, Publish with data-primary on Publish — reserving its band in real layout with a padding-bottom on .b-field equal to its height, exactly as [data-medium] .b-field[data-editor-open] already reserves the sheet, so it never floats over a row. Stack it directly above the reversibility bar's bottom-edge position rather than sharing that node, and add its height to the bar's offset so the two can never overlap (the .b-edit bottom:76px rule at b.css:938 is the pattern to copy). Leave the workspace line and the identity capsule in .b-bar. That puts the count, the day, the today line and two moments on the owner's first screen. Gate: assert at 390 on owner-flight that at least two .b-item boxes are inside the viewport on first paint, that all three verbs are still reachable by keyboard, and that no .b-item is overlapped by the action row at any scroll position.

biggestWin: The owner half of this product is now finished and honest, and that is what moved it from 6.6 to 7.5. Everything a planner can do, they can now undo: Add a moment creates a real empty moment, names it as you type and disappears on Ctrl Z; Delete restores the row at its own index and puts focus back on it; a date can be typed in words or nudged by a week; Shown and Hidden say which they are in the row, in the accessible name and in the reversibility bar. The ceremony has one true action, an inert line where sending is not built, and a way home. The editor is a rail at 1280 and a sheet below it, and the reversibility bar travels with it without ever standing over the measure. The measure itself remains the best idea in the lab: real days at real distance, anchored by TODAY IS 16 JULY, with the empty stretch named rather than closed up. What stands between this and 9.5 is not the direction — I would not reopen it — and it is not polish. It is two builds and one decision, roughly three days. Fund the session list first: until Preview shows the plan as edited, the owner's core loop silently destroys work and misreports what guests will see, and that is the defect most likely to lose a customer in week one. Second is the past block, which got built closed in the two rooms where it should fold and broken in the two where it should be open — the record room and the printed keepsake delete the heading, the count and every row, and the gate passes because its only assertion checks that the control is gone. The decision is the wedding morning: on the day, the artifact every guest opens holds 214 characters, states that it is the day, and offers a list of things already finished. Either the data model carries the running order of the day and that screen becomes the best thing in the product, or it does not and the screen should say so plainly. It currently does neither, and it is the screen the whole company will be judged by.
